summary: Executed the live install -> load -> upgrade -> reload -> uninstall verification against the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 (musl) host at http://127.0.0.1:8096 (GET /System/Info/Public reports Version 12.0.0). The verification work is complete, but Phase 7 acceptance criterion 2 is NOT met because a release-blocking defect was found, so ready_for_next_task is false. Package: `. /config/arrtags-env.sh && ./build.sh package` produced artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip (5,475,291 bytes) containing ArrTags.dll, SkiaSharp.dll, libSkiaSharp.so, ArrTags.deps.json, build.yaml, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md and licenses/ (9 entries). Plugin layout: the host's actual plugin path was determined empirically to be <prefix>/data/plugins (Jellyfin's ProgramDataPath/--datadir), NOT <prefix>/config/plugins as the committed test-host doc claimed; the .jellyfin-plugin marker and the data/plugins/configurations/ directory (built-in plugin XMLs) confirm it, and InstallationManager installs a repository package to data/plugins/<Name>_<Version>/. Install: extracted the package to /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0 and restarted via scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh /tmp/jf; the console logged 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0', the host wrote an Active meta.json (guid 40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46, targetAbi 12.0.0.0, version 0.1.0.0) and plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml, and reached 'Startup complete' with no [ERR]/[FTL] lines. Because the plugin is constructed through ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance(IServiceProvider, Plugin) and the plugin instance was actually created (not merely present on disk), this validates the pinned-host load of the Plugin(IServiceProvider) constructor (Phase 5 carry-forward). Upgrade: temporarily set version 0.1.0.1 in Directory.Build.props and build.yaml via sed, built and packaged artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.1.zip, installed it alongside 0.1.0.0, restarted, and confirmed the host loaded only 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.1' and auto-deleted the older ArrTags_0.1.0.0 folder (versioned-install-folder behavior). All temporary version edits were reverted with `git checkout -- build.yaml Directory.Build.props` (repo back at 0.1.0.0) and the temporary 0.1.0.1 artifact was removed. Reload: Jellyfin has no in-process plugin reload, so restart is the reload mechanism; a restart reloaded ArrTags exactly once (grep count 1), with no duplicate registrations and 'Startup complete'. Uninstall: removing the plugin folder and restarting produced zero ArrTags loads, no ArrTags log lines, no errors and 'Startup complete'. RELEASE BLOCKER (Phase 7 acceptance criterion 2 not met): Jellyfin derives a plugin's DataFolderPath as PluginsPath/Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(assembly.Location) - proved with a task-owned net10.0 probe that references the release /tmp/jf/jellyfin/MediaBrowser.Common.dll and mimics the ArrTags assembly name, yielding DataFolderPath = <PluginsPath>/ArrTags whether or not that directory exists. The plugin persists its state under that folder, so once it has written any state (metadata state, artwork operations, lifecycle fence, or source artifacts) a data/plugins/ArrTags directory exists. When that data folder is present alongside the standard versioned install folder data/plugins/ArrTags_<version>/, PluginManager.DiscoverPlugins groups both by the identical manifest name 'ArrTags' and, because the auto-manifest GUID for a folder without meta.json is MD5('ArrTags') = 62a5f130-6c8e-59dd-cdcc-3e1a380fd309 which sorts after the real plugin GUID 40322d52-5680-449f-b33e-e01836ee2f46, keeps the data folder and deletes the install folder, so no ArrTags plugin is loaded. This was reproduced cleanly A/B/A with the committed 0.1.0.0 package: with no data folder the plugin loads; after creating data/plugins/ArrTags/authoritative/sentinel.json the next restart deletes ArrTags_0.1.0.0 and loads nothing (sentinel survives); removing the data folder and reinstalling makes it load again. The unversioned layout data/plugins/ArrTags/ (install folder == data folder) plus a persisted state file also loads exactly once and preserves the state, and the no-state versioned case is fine - so the defect is specific to the collision between the versioned install layout and the Jellyfin-derived data folder. Exercising Plugin.OnUninstalling live requires an authenticated elevated uninstall (DELETE /Plugins/<guid>/<version> returns HTTP 401 while StartupWizardCompleted is false and no API key exists), so it was not exercised; the drain is covered in-process by LifecycleFoundationTests.PluginUninstallHook* and ArtworkLifecycleTests. Live ImageSaver read-back could not be exercised (the host has no media library item, and creating one needs a library, a media file and a scan); the existing task 5.11 read-back uses a DispatchProxy IProviderManager rather than the real host ImageSaver, so it remains open. Host-guarded suite: ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR=/tmp/jf/jellyfin ./build.sh test reported Failed 0, Passed 1229, Skipped 44, Total 1273 (the 14 newly-run facts are the 9 JellyfinImageResponseTests and 5 JellyfinImageRouteTests that reflect over Jellyfin.Api.dll); the default ./build.sh test behaviour is unchanged at Failed 0, Passed 1215, Skipped 58, Total 1273. The host was returned to a clean, safe state (no ArrTags install folder, no data folder, config XML removed, host running and reaching Startup complete). Documentation updated: corrected the plugins path in docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md and scripts/provision-jellyfin-test-host.sh, and recorded the verification and the blocker in PLANS.md, docs/changelog.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/implementation-readiness.md.

DataFolderPath proof: task-owned net10.0 console project (/tmp/7.2/datapathprobe, AssemblyName=ArrTags) referencing the release /tmp/jf/jellyfin/MediaBrowser.Common.dll and MediaBrowser.Model.dll, with DispatchProxy IApplicationPaths/IXmlSerializer; output 'DataFolderPath = <pluginsPath>/ArrTags' for both a nonexistent and an existing ArrTags directory (no _<version> suffix).

Unversioned layout probe: /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags/ (install folder == data folder) with a persisted authoritative/sentinel.json loaded exactly once ('Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0') and preserved the sentinel across restart.

known_limitations: RELEASE BLOCKER (Phase 7 acceptance criterion 2 not met): the standard versioned install layout (PluginsPath/<Name>_<Version>, which is what Jellyfin's InstallationManager produces for a repository install) becomes unsafe once the plugin has persisted any state. The plugin's Jellyfin-derived DataFolderPath is PluginsPath/<assembly name> = data/plugins/ArrTags; when that data folder is present alongside data/plugins/ArrTags_<version>/, PluginManager.DiscoverPlugins treats them as two versions of the same-named plugin and, because the folder-derived auto-manifest GUID MD5('ArrTags') sorts after the real plugin GUID, deletes the install folder and loads no ArrTags plugin on the next restart. Fixing this needs a production or installation-layout decision and was deliberately not implemented in this verification task. The unversioned layout data/plugins/ArrTags/ is unaffected (but then state lives inside the install folder, so replacing the folder loses provenance).
No live Sonarr or Radarr instance was exercised; only the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host was live, consistent with the test-host documentation.

The live Plugin.OnUninstalling drain was not exercised: PluginsController requires the RequiresElevation policy (HTTP 401) and StartupWizardCompleted is false, so no authenticated admin uninstall is possible without completing the setup wizard (host user state beyond this task's scope). The drain remains covered in-process by LifecycleFoundationTests.PluginUninstallHookResolvesTheCoordinatorAndDrainsTheUninstallFence / PluginUninstallHookContainsACoordinatorFailure / PluginUninstallHookIsSafeWithoutAResolvableCoordinator and by ArtworkLifecycleTests (uninstall-fence drain and restoration cases).

Live ImageSaver read-back fidelity (Phase 5 carry-forward) could not be exercised without a real media library item: the pinned host has no library, no media file and StartupWizardCompleted false, and creating a library item requires a library, a media file and a scan. The task 5.11 in-process publish-then-read-back uses the real ArrTags image-mutation boundary but a DispatchProxy IProviderManager instead of the real host ImageSaver, so the real ImageSaver on-disk representation remains unverified live.

The upgrade test required a temporary 0.1.0.1 version bump in Directory.Build.props and build.yaml; it was reverted with `git checkout -- build.yaml Directory.Build.props` (repo confirmed back at 0.1.0.0) and the temporary artifact was deleted, so the committed repository stays at 0.1.0.0. The upgrade moved from 0.1.0.0 to 0.1.0.1 only; no other version-change path was tested.

The data-folder collision and the `Directory.EnumerateDirectories(root, "*.*")` dotless-name matching were verified on this net10.0 runtime and the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 build only; the ordering depends on MD5('ArrTags') comparing after the plugin GUID and on meta.json being absent from the data folder, both of which hold here.

The final host state has the plugin uninstalled (clean) rather than installed; the positive install/load evidence is recorded in this report and in the host console log excerpts under /tmp/7.2/evidence during the run (the temporary evidence directory is removed at task completion).

The pinned test host runs with --nowebclient and StartupWizardCompleted false, so no dynamic/authenticated API surface (plugin list, uninstall, image route over HTTP) was exercised; only filesystem install lifecycle, console logging and the unauthenticated /System/Info/Public endpoint were used.
